slides.headline: Over 50 and never lifted a weight?
slides.sub: Strength is trainable at any age. Here's a simple way to start.

slides.title: Why strength matters more now
slides.body: Muscle and bone keep responding to load throughout life. Research suggests strength training can help with everyday tasks, balance and joint pain, and it's rarely too late to start.

slides.title: Pick four or five basic moves
slides.body: Sit-to-stands, wall push-ups, step-ups, band rows and calf raises cover most of the body. You don't need a gym to begin, just a chair, a step and a resistance band.

slides.title: Twice a week is a great start
slides.body: Two sessions a week of 20 to 30 minutes is enough for most people to feel a difference. Aim for 8 to 12 reps, where the last few feel challenging but controlled.

slides.title: Some stiffness is normal
slides.body: Feeling a bit stiff a day or two later is common when you start. If a joint aches, adjust the load or range rather than stopping altogether, and progress over weeks.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness with exercise needs a GP review. If a joint swells or pain builds session after session, see a physio to adjust your program.

slides.body: Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios build strength programs around your joints, your history and your goals. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Never lifted a weight and wondering if you've left it too late? You haven't.

Muscle and bone respond to load at any age, and research suggests strength training can make everyday life easier, from carrying shopping to getting up off the floor.

Start simple: four or five moves like sit-to-stands, wall push-ups and step-ups, twice a week, with the last few reps feeling challenging. A bit of stiffness the next day is common. Adjust and keep going rather than stopping. If you have heart or health concerns, check in with your GP first.

story.headline: Over 50 and new to weights?
story.body: Try sit-to-stands, wall push-ups and step-ups twice a week. Start easy, build slowly.
